questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: (1) Following an exhaustive investigation into the internal network systems, / (2) the expert technicians reported that the root cause of the data breach / (3) was because an administrative employee had inadvertently clicked / (4) on a highly sophisticated phishing hyperlink.
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(1) Following an exhaustive investigation into the internal network systems, / (2) the expert technicians reported that the root cause of the data breach / (3) was because an administrative employee had inadvertently clicked / (4) on a highly sophisticated phishing hyperlink.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. was because .

Key Points

  • The phrase "was because" is grammatically incorrect and considered redundant. Instead of saying "was because," one should use "was due to" or "was caused by."
  • The correct usage in this context would be: "was due to an administrative employee..." to maintain proper grammar and clarity.
  • Using "because" directly after "was" is a common error and should be avoided as it disrupts the logical flow of the sentence.

Correct sentence: Following an exhaustive investigation into the internal network systems, the expert technicians reported that the root cause of the data breach was due to an administrative employee inadvertently clicking on a highly sophisticated phishing hyperlink.

Additional Information

  • Common Error with "because":
    • The phrase "was because" is incorrect because "was" implies a state or result, while "because" introduces a reason. Instead, use "was due to" or "was caused by" for clarity.
    • Example: Incorrect: "The issue was because of poor planning."
      Correct: "The issue was due to poor planning."
  • Tips for Avoiding Redundancy:
    • Eliminate unnecessary words or phrases that repeat the same meaning.
    • Replace incorrect combinations like "was because" with grammatically correct alternatives.

The correct answer is '1' i.e. I, after having conferred .

Key Points

  • The sentence contains an error in the use of the pronoun "myself."
  • The reflexive pronoun "myself" is used when the subject and the object of the action are the same person, or for emphasis. In this case, it is incorrectly used as a substitute for the pronoun "I."
  • The correct subject pronoun to use alongside "the architect" is "I."
  • Thus, the corrected sentence should replace "myself" with "I."

Correct sentence: The architect and I, after having conferred with the structural engineers, decided that the cantilevered roof required additional reinforcement.

Additional Information

  • Reflexive Pronouns: Reflexive pronouns such as "myself," "yourself," "himself," etc., are used in two cases:
    • When the subject and the object are the same. Example: I hurt myself.
    • For emphasis. Example: I did it myself.
  • In this sentence, "myself" is neither fulfilling the above conditions nor replacing the correct subject pronoun.
  • Therefore, option 1 (I, after having conferred) is the grammatically correct choice.

questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: (1) The technical efficiency of the prototype hydrogen-fuel-cell propulsion system / (2) is at least as optimal, if not more optimal than, the standard lithium-ion / (3) configurations currently used by automotive manufacturers / (4) across the European market.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. is at least as optimal, if not more optimal than .

Key Points

  • The error in the sentence lies in the phrase "is at least as optimal, if not more optimal than."
  • The word "optimal" is an absolute adjective, which means it does not have comparative or superlative forms. "Optimal" implies the highest or best possible, so phrases like "more optimal" or "most optimal" are considered redundant and incorrect.
  • The correct form of the phrase should be "is at least as optimal as the standard lithium-ion configurations...".

Correct sentence: The technical efficiency of the prototype hydrogen-fuel-cell propulsion system is at least as optimal as the standard lithium-ion configurations currently used by automotive manufacturers across the European market.

Additional Information

  • Absolute Adjectives:
    • Adjectives like "perfect," "unique," "optimal," and "absolute" are considered absolute and do not take comparative or superlative forms.
    • Example of incorrect usage: "more perfect," "most unique," "more optimal."
    • Example of correct usage: "This design is optimal for the given conditions."
  • Common Errors to Avoid:
    • Using redundant comparative forms with absolute adjectives.
    • Example: "This machine is more optimal than the other." (Incorrect)
    • Corrected: "This machine is optimal for the task compared to the other."

Key Points

  • The given sentence is in the active voice, and we have to convert it into the passive voice.

​Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 3".

S1. Species are going extinct at an unprecedented rate.

P.  The sharpest declines have occurred throughout the world’s rivers and lakes, where freshwater wildlife has plummeted by 84% since 1970 – about 4% per year.

Q. As more and more species are drawn towards extinction, the very life support systems on which civilization depends are eroded.

S. Wildlife populations have fallen by more than two-thirds over the last 50 years, according to a new report from the World Wildlife Fund.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'SPQR'.

Key Points

  •  While arranging the parts of the passage, we should find some grammatical or contextual connections between them-
    • S follows sentence 1 as the phrase 'Wildlife populations have fallen' mentioned in 'S' refers back to "extinct" in sentence 1.
    • Next is P as the 'fall of wildlife population' mentioned in S is further described in P.
    • After that is Q as it describes the effect of 'wildlife population decline' mentioned in 'P'.
    • Last is R as the noun 'threat' mentioned in R is linked with the 'threats' mentioned in sentence 6.

P. The sharpest declines have occurred throughout the world’s rivers and lakes, where freshwater wildlife has plummeted by 84% since 1970 – about 4% per year.

questions.question: The Shisht Bharat campaign, launched by an NGO, aims to strengthen the moral character of Indian citizens by _______ them about values of morality, civic sense, politeness, decorum and dignity.
questions.questionHtml: The Shisht Bharat campaign, launched by an NGO, aims to strengthen the moral character of Indian citizens by _______ them about values of morality, civic sense, politeness, decorum and dignity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1.

The word 'vocalising' means 'uttering (a sound or a word)'. This is incorrect because this makes the sentence grammatically incorrect as well as meaningless. This is because mere utterance of values to people will not serve the purpose of the campaign.

The word 'demarcating' means 'separating or distinguishing'. This is incorrect because the word 'demarcating' does not fit the context.

The word 'informing' means 'give (someone) facts or information; tell'. The word 'sensitizing' means 'cause (someone or something) to respond to certain stimuli; make sensitive'. Both these words make the sentence meaningful as well as grammatically correct. However, the latter fits the context more appropriately. The task of the campaign is to arouse or stimulate moral values among the citizens. For this mere 'informing' is not enough, rather 'sensitizing' them about moral values is needed.

Hence, the correct word will be 'sensitizing'.

The correct sentence is: The Shisht Bharat campaign, launched by an NGO, aims to strengthen the moral character of Indian citizens by sensitizing them about values of morality, civic sense, politeness, decorum and dignity.

questions.question: ​Launched initially in Delhi NCR, the campaign brings together policy-makers, media personalities, parents, RWAs, Delhi traffic police, NGOs, corporate houses and multinationals together for the _______ of the cause.

The word 'vigilance' means 'the action or state of keeping careful watch for possible danger or difficulties'. This does not fit the context.

The word 'degradation' means 'the condition or process of lowering the quality of (something)'. This is incorrect because the campaign would not bring together people to degrade its cause. Rather, people must further the cause of the campaign. 

The word 'silence' means 'cause to become silent; prohibit or prevent from speaking'. This is incorrect because the noble cause of the campaign is not to be silenced, rather it is to be promoted.

The correct word is 'promoting' which means 'support or actively encourage (a cause, venture, etc.); further the progress of'. The sentence conveys the meaning that so many people have been brought together by the campaign so that the cause of making people morally sensitive is promoted and made successful.

The correct sentence is: Launched initially in Delhi NCR, the campaign brings together policy-makers, media personalities, parents, RWAs, Delhi traffic police, NGOs, corporate houses and multinationals together for the promotion of the cause.

questions.question: The Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) Development of North-Eastern Region (DoNER), MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr Jitendra Singh said that the elders should set an example in their conduct before the younger generation, so that the youth can inherit these values naturally by _______ their elder generations
questions.questionHtml: The  Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) Development of North-Eastern Region (DoNER), MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr Jitendra Singh said that the elders should set an example in their conduct before the younger generation,  so that the youth can inherit these values naturally by _______ their elder generations
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2.

The word 'respecting' means 'admire (someone or something) deeply, as a result of their abilities, qualities, or achievements'. This is incorrect. The phrase 'set an example means 'behave in a way that others find good and copy'. One might respect elders and still not imitate their good qualities.

The word 'empathising' means 'understanding the feeling of another'. This is incorrect because it does not justify the phrase 'set an example'. 

The word 'symbolising' means 'represent by means of a symbol'. This does not fit the context.

The correct word is 'emulating' which means 'match or surpass (a person or achievement), typically by imitation'. This justifies the phrase 'set an example'. The Minister had said that the conduct of elders should be such that the younger generations imitate them.

The correct sentence is: The  Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) Development of North-Eastern Region (DoNER), MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr Jitendra Singh said that the elders should set an example in their conduct before the younger generation,  so that the youth can inherit these values naturally by emulating their elder generations.

questions.question: ​He added that our ancient scriptures describe that it takes three generations for values to change, so _______ efforts are needed to inculcate good values in our coming generations.
questions.questionHtml: ​He added that our ancient scriptures describe that it takes three generations for values to change, so _______ efforts are needed to inculcate good values in our coming generations.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2.

Note that the word 'so' before the blank is used for conjunction. Therefore, what is said in the second clause (after 'so') should be a result of what is said in the first clause (before 'so').

The word 'gullible' means 'easily persuaded to believe something; credulous'. This does not make a meaningful sentence and therefore it is incorrect.

The word 'complicated' means 'intricate'. This is incorrect because nothing in the passage suggests that intricate efforts are needed to inculcate good values in the coming generations.

The word 'cautious' means 'careful to avoid potential problems or dangers'. This does not fit the context.

The correct word is 'Consistent' which means 'acting or done in the same way over time'. The sentence means that changes in values come over time and therefore, consistent effort is required.

The correct sentence is: He added that our ancient scriptures describe that it takes three generations for values to change, so consistent efforts are needed to inculcate good values in our coming generations.

questions.question: The Minister said that such kind of campaigns help in _______ the masses in a positive direction.

The word 'detouring' means 'take a long or roundabout route'. This is incorrect because it does not fit the context.

The word 'originating' means 'have a specified beginning'. This is also incorrect because it does not fit the context.

The word 'determining' means 'cause (something) to occur in a particular way or to have a particular nature'. This is incorrect because it does not make a meaningful sentence.

The correct word is 'channelizing' which means 'to guide or direct towards'. The sentence conveys the meaning that campaigns like the 'Shisht Bharat campaign' help in guiding the masses in a positive direction.

The correct sentence is: The Minister said that such kind of campaigns help in channelizing the masses in a positive direction.
